title: Reporting standard and error bars: paired, co-scheduled stage tables with noise-floor, power, truncation/unknown bounds and an occasion audit (implemented and verified on cal-1/v3 training cells)
verdict_cn:
结论：可行，已经做好并核对过。

我做了每个阶段五个评测集的标准结果表，以及配套的计算程序（只用基础数值库）。用校准实验 cal-1（同样 200 道训练题、11 种提示文字、每题跑 4 次）核对：10 组对比的平均差、95% 区间、变好/变差题数和检验概率，与事先登记的分析逐位一致。

表的规矩：每个评测集给出两组同题配对差：
- 比"不加技能文字"（技能文字，即附加在系统提示里的经验文字）；
- 比"任务说明起点"。

每组差都带区间、变好/变差题数和精确检验。另列"同一文字重跑的噪声范围"和"能检出的最小效果"，再单列回答被截断的次数、没出结果的格数，以及它们可能造成的上下限。

两个新发现：
1. 同样的请求在不同时间段会得到"简短"或"啰嗦"两种回答状态。在 OfficeQA（文档问答）上，同一文字、同样 60 题，分数差了 22 到 24 个百分点。所以比较的双方必须在同一时间段交错运行，否则不给区间。
2. 无关的占位文字本身就让分数变化 −9.8 到 +3.6 个百分点，远大于同一文字重跑的 ±2.2。

按现有题量，单个评测集只能可靠检出约 3.5 到 10 个百分点的效果，五个评测集平均约 3.8 个百分点。

建议主会话先用我的程序，检查 v3（第三版正式运行）的测试格是不是同一时间段跑的，再出表。
what_i_did:
I made zero model calls and used training cells only: cal-1 SearchQA training items, and the v3 train/selftest/screen/confirm rounds. I listed, opened or copied no test, holdout or evaluation path.

(1) Audited and reused an earlier, interrupted D11 attempt found in this scratchpad folder (extracts, library, analyses; there was no report).
- The extracts match the machines byte for byte in size: cal1_cells_v2.tsv is 2,488,409 bytes on the old machine and v3_train_cells.tsv is 3,804,714 bytes on the new one.
- The extractor globs only {train,selftest,screen,confirm} units and refuses test-like paths.
- I re-ran its suite: 42/42 pass.
- I corrected its Miller equation citations: the paired SE is Eq. 7 (not 5) and the clustered SE is Eq. 4 (not 8).

(2) New analyses, all in scratchpad/feas/D11/scripts2:
- request_identity.py: byte identity of requests across rounds.
- serving_modes.py and mode_timeline.py: serving-regime signatures over time and per arm inside rounds.
- regime_interaction.py: whether an effect estimate changes with the occasion, paired over items.
- projections.py: test-size noise floors and detectable effects.

(3) Built the template implementation:
- stage_table.py: paired Δ vs NoSkill and vs Seed, CR1-clustered t intervals, Tango/Newcombe/bootstrap cross-checks, exact sign-flip p with Holm, noise floor, MDE80, truncation and unknown bounds, co-scheduling audit, macro row.
- Adapters: cells_to_long.py (coevo5 cell JSON to long TSV, for the main session's evaluation cells) and to_long.py.
- verify_vs_registered.py: checks the output against the registered analysis.

(4) Verified the literature claims against the sources: arXiv HTML and abstract pages for Miller 2024, Bowyer et al. 2025, Madaan et al. 2024 and Chen et al. 2023; the Thinking Machines post (He et al. 2025); and the Newcombe 1998 PDF.

(5) Ran everything end to end on the new machine: raw cell JSON, then long TSV, then table.

The task asked for report.md on the Mac. The harness refused the write with "Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files", so I did not work around it. The full report content is in the fields below.
evidence:
All items below are MEASURED on training cells unless marked otherwise.

A. cal-1 (200 SearchQA training items × 4 runs × 11 arms, all interleaved 10-20 16:07-19:52)
- Dispatch: 8,800/8,800 cells have verdicts; 15 unknown runs; 8 truncated runs.
- Single-run same-text disagreement π_rep and ICC:
  - parent:A: 0.119 (198 complete items), ICC 0.73
  - parent:B: 0.104 (198), ICC 0.76
  - parent:A and B pooled over 8 runs: 0.1075 (196)
  - ids-full: 0.049 (199), ICC 0.86
  - seed-only: 0.052
  - placebos: 0.074-0.161
  - cand: 0.157
  - So the task card halves the run noise.
- Same text dispatched twice (parent:B − parent:A, registered convention): +0.75 [−1.25, +2.75], 22 up / 18 down / 160 tie, p = 0.64.
- Design effect, naive cell-level unpaired SE ÷ item-paired SE: 2.29 (same text), 1.23 (control:3), 1.01 (ids-full). The naive SE is wrong in either direction.
- Runs per item, ids-full − parent:A over 197 items. Empirical SE: K=1 2.82, K=2 2.44, K=4 2.22 points. Projected MDE80 at n = 400: 5.6 / 4.8 / 4.4. At K=1, 52% of the variance is run noise and ω² = 0.077 is item-level effect heterogeneity. For the same text the SE falls 2.41 → 1.01.
- Placebos vs parent:A:

  | Placebo | Δ [95% CI] | Up / down |
  |---|---|---|
  | control:1 | −3.5 [−6.3, −0.7] | 20/33 |
  | control:2 | +3.6 [+0.6, +6.6] | 39/16, p = 0.0027 |
  | control:3 | −9.75 [−13.6, −5.9] | 16/58 |
  | control:4 | +0.25 [−2.8, +3.3] | |

- Rule-shaped arms sit inside the placebo range: seed-rule +0.4 [−3.1, +3.9]; seed-rule3 −3.0 [−6.6, +0.6]; cand −2.6 [−7.2, +2.0].
- The full task card is far outside it: ids-full +9.4 [+5.1, +13.7]; seed-only +8.9 [+5.1, +12.7].

B. Interval coverage
- Single-run paired tables (the test-table case), exact enumeration over 40 grid points: n ∈ {125, 172, 279, 400} × discordance {8, 16, 30%} × true Δ {0, 3, 8 points}, plus n ∈ {20, 50}.
  - n ≥ 125: Wald-t 94.6-95.7%, Tango 94.2-95.7%, Newcombe-10 94.9-96.0%, percentile bootstrap 93.3-95.9%.
  - n = 20: Wald-t 91.7-96.6%, bootstrap 90.6-96.4%, Tango 95.2-96.8%.
- Gate-panel sizes, items resampled from the cal-1 bank (4,000 simulations each):

  | n | Paired t | Percentile bootstrap |
  |---|---|---|
  | 6 | 73-95% | 48-83% |
  | 11 | 91-96% | 69-88% |
  | 20 | 93-96% | 85-93% |
  | ≥ 100 | about 95% | about 95% |

- Conclusion: frequentist paired intervals are fine at stage-table sizes. The bootstrap must never be used on trigger panels. This agrees with Bowyer et al. 2025 at small n.

C. Occasion (serving-regime) effects
- Requests are byte-identical. Over 9,707 first sends in 1,213 (Skill text, item) pairs that recur in ≥ 2 rounds or arms, 0 pairs have more than one request SHA-256.
- Regimes alternate in time. Terse share = cells with ≤ 12 completion tokens, all arms, per 15-minute bin:

  | Bench | Window (HKT) | Terse share | Pass |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | SearchQA | 10-19 23:15-23:45 | 5-9% | |
  | SearchQA | 10-20 00:00-01:15 | 60-80% | |
  | SearchQA | 10-20 01:30-02:00 | 17-44% | |
  | SearchQA | 10-20 02:15-09:45 | 69-96% | |
  | SearchQA | 10-20 10:00 | 15% | |
  | SearchQA | cal-1, 15:45-19:45 | 17-27% | |
  | OfficeQA | 01:00 | 69% | 25% |
  | OfficeQA | 01:30-02:00 | 6-18% | 39-55% |
  | OfficeQA | 02:15-04:45 | 70-81% | 15-35% |
  | OfficeQA | 10:00 | 8% | 52% |

- No reasoning characters were returned, and returned_model was always deepseek-v4-flash. The cause is UNKNOWN.
- Same text, same items, identical requests, different windows:

  | Text and items | Comparison | Δ [95% CI] |
  |---|---|---|
  | Seed, 60 OfficeQA | s3 screen (01:35-02:04) − s2 train (01:03-01:07); 50.8% vs 28.3% | +22.5 [+11.5, +33.5] |
  | Seed, 60 OfficeQA | s3 screen − s4 screen | +24.2 [+12.6, +35.7] |
  | Seed, 60 OfficeQA | s4 screen vs s4 confirm (both terse) | 0.0 [−6.7, +6.7] |
  | Scaffold, 200 SearchQA | v3 E-ds s1 train (terse) − cal-1 parent:A | +6.1 [+2.1, +10.2] |
  | Scaffold, 200 SearchQA | s1 screen − s1 train | −5.6 [−9.7, −1.6] |
  | Seed, 200 SearchQA | v3 vs cal-1 | +0.1 [−1.7, +2.0] |

- The regime interacts with the text. Seed − scaffold on the same 200 SearchQA items is +3.25 [−0.39, +6.89] when the arms ran in different windows, and +9.25 [+4.91, +13.59] in cal-1 where they were interleaved. The paired difference of the two estimates is −6.00 [−10.45, −1.55], sign-flip p = 0.009.
- Inside rounds the arms are interleaved: E-ds s1 screen, 9 arms over 01:07-02:03 with median starts 01:32-01:40; I-ds s1 screen, 8 arms over 00:20-01:03 with medians 00:41-00:43. Within-round gate contrasts were protected by time. Cross-round, cross-chain and differently-timed test comparisons were not.

D. v3 own-stage train rounds, task-card seed (I-ds) vs empty scaffold (E-ds). Not co-scheduled: window overlap 0% on all five benches.

  | Bench | Δ [95% CI] | Up / down |
  |---|---|---|
  | SearchQA | +3.2 [−0.4, +6.9] | 20/11 |
  | OfficeQA, 74 items in 54 clusters | +4.7 [−1.5, +10.9] | 9/5 |
  | LiveMath | −4.5 [−10.2, +1.2] | 9/15 |
  | SpreadsheetBench, n = 89 known, 1 run | +1.1 [−8.7, +10.9] | 10/9 |
  | ALFWorld | +10.5 [+2.3, +18.7] | 12/3; raw p 0.021, Holm 0.10 |
  | Macro | +3.0 [−0.1, +6.1] | |

- OfficeQA clustering barely matters here: SE 3.22 for independent items, 3.08 for Miller Eq. 4 and 3.08 for CR1 (design effect 0.92).

E. Verification of the implementation
- test_d11stats.py: 42/42 checks pass. They cover Newcombe Table III (15 configurations, 4 decimals); Tango = repo matched.paired_difference (max |Δ| 5.0e-07); the sign test = repo matched.sign_test_p and coevo5.stats.sign_test (exact); the paired-SE identities; and simulated variance components.
- verify_vs_registered.py: with the registered convention (unknown = fail), all 10 contrasts vs parent:A match cal1_analyse.py in mean, CI to 4 decimals, up/down/tie and sign p. The contrasts are ids-full, seed-only, seed-rule, seed-rule3, cand, parent:B and control:1-4.
- The end-to-end run on the new machine from raw cell JSON reproduces Demo B's SearchQA row.

F. ESTIMATED projections to test panels (single run; test denominators from docs/handoff/coevo5-v1-results-20261019.md)

  | Bench | Noise floor (±) | MDE80 (points) |
  |---|---|---|
  | SearchQA, n = 400 | 2.5 | 3.5-4.4 |
  | OfficeQA, 172 | 4.4 | 6.3-7.4 |
  | LiveMath, 125 | 6.7 | 9.5-9.8 |
  | SpreadsheetBench, about 200 qualified (π borrowed from about 15 items, weak) | 6.2 | 8.9-9.2 |
  | ALFWorld, 134 | 6.3 | 9.1-9.9 |
  | Equal-weight macro | 2.4-2.6 | 3.5-3.8 |

- The earlier learned-clause effects of +3 to +5 points (claim, context §3) lie below every per-bench detectable effect.
design:
TEMPLATE: one table per (chain, stage) on the test panels.

Arms per bench, dispatched INTERLEAVED in one window:
- NoSkill;
- Seed (the task-card seed);
- Final (the Skill after this stage);
- optionally Rep (a same-window replicate of one arm), for the noise-floor line;
- at the final stage, Placebo (Seed plus length-matched irrelevant text).

Columns:

| Bench | n (G) | K | NoSkill % | Seed % | Final % | Δ vs NoSkill [95% CI] (up/down; p_Holm) | Δ vs Seed [95% CI] (up/down; p_Holm) | Noise floor ± | MDE80 | Trunc F/N/S | Unknown F/N/S | Co-scheduled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Then one macro row per reference, then a detail block per bench: exact Δ as a fraction, SE, cluster bootstrap, raw p, unknown and truncation bounds, 2×2 table with Tango and Newcombe-10 when K = 1, and per-arm window, median completion tokens, terse share and Wilson interval.

RULES
- R1 Unit. The item is the unit. For OfficeQA, items sharing a source file form one cluster (union-find, as in readout.panel). Runs are averaged within an item, never treated as independent.
- R2 Primary quantity. The paired difference on the same items. Arm accuracies are secondary (Wilson 95% interval when K = 1). The current reports show per-arm intervals only.
- R3 Interval. Paired t with df = G − 1 on the CR1 cluster-robust SE. Cross-checks: the shared-draw cluster bootstrap (what readout.Readings already does), and Tango or Newcombe-10 when K = 1. If fewer than 10 items are discordant, Tango is primary.
- R4 Counts and test. Report up/down/tie. The p-value is the exact two-sided paired sign-flip test (= exact McNemar when K = 1). Holm over the 10 Δ cells of the table.
- R5 Noise floor. Take π_rep from a same-window replicate, else from within-arm run pairs, else a borrowed calibration value marked *. The band is ±1.96 sqrt(π_rep/(K n)). MDE80 = 2.80 × SE. A Δ inside the band is described as "within noise".
- R6 Unknowns. Excluded from the primary estimate. Report counts and the low/high bounds; flag a cell as "unknown-sensitive" when the bounds change the conclusion.
- R7 Truncations. Count as fail, as the scorer does. Report counts and the truncation bounds; flag as "truncation-sensitive" when they matter.
- R8 Co-scheduling. Record windows and serving signatures. When windows overlap by less than 80%, print "not co-scheduled, no CI" and re-run interleaved. Cells reused because the Skill is unchanged are printed "reused, Δ ≡ 0 by construction", never "+0.0 [0, 0]".
- R9 Macro. Equal-weight mean, SE = sqrt(Σ SE_b²)/5, plus the stratified bootstrap.
- R10 Transfer and no-drop. On registered similar targets, Δ vs Seed counts as transfer only if the lower 95% bound is above 0. On dissimilar benches, compare the lower bound with the registered non-inferiority margin (from D8).
- R11 Placebo line at the final stage. Learned content must beat Seed + placebo.
- R12 Denominators always shown: n, G, K, cells, unknown, truncated, and qualification exclusions.

FORMULAS
- Item score: s_{A,i} = mean_k y_{A,i,k}. Difference: d_i = s_{F,i} − s_{R,i}. Estimate: Δ̂ = (1/n) Σ_i d_i (exact Fraction).
- Independent items, Miller Eq. 7: SE = sqrt(Σ (d_i − Δ̂)² / (n(n − 1))). For K = 1: SE² = ((f + g) − (f − g)²/n) / (n(n − 1)).
- CR1: SE = (1/n) sqrt(G/(G − 1) · Σ_g (Σ_{i∈g} (d_i − Δ̂))²). Miller Eq. 4 is the same sum without the factor and with 1/(n − 1) on the diagonal.
- CI: Δ̂ ± t_{.975, G−1} SE.
- Tango: {δ : |f − g − nδ| / sqrt(n(2q̂ + δ(1 − δ))) ≤ 1.96}.
- Sign-flip: p = P(|Σ ε_i d_i| ≥ |Σ d_i|). Exact up to 20 non-zero d_i, else Monte Carlo with 200,000 draws.
- Holm: p_(j)^adj = max_{l ≤ j} min(1, (m − l + 1) p_(l)).
- Variance components:
  - σ²_w = mean_i of the within-item run variance (ddof 1);
  - Var(x) = S²(s_i) − σ²_w/K;
  - π_rep = 2σ²_w;
  - ω² = S²(d_i) − σ²_wF/K_F − σ²_wR/K_R;
  - projected SE(n, K) = sqrt((ω² + σ²_wF/K + σ²_wR/K)/n);
  - MDE80 = (1.95996 + 0.84162) SE (Miller Eq. 10).
- Noise floor: Var(D) = π_rep/(K n).
- Unknown and truncation bounds: [CI_low(Final worst, reference best), CI_high(Final best, reference worst)].

IMPLEMENTATION
- Library: scripts/d11stats.py (numpy, math, fractions; no scipy).
- Table: scripts2/stage_table.py. Usage:
  `python3 -I -B stage_table.py CELLS.tsv --final F --noskill N --seed T [--replicate REP=SAME] [--clusters officeqa=files.json] [--borrow-pi bench=v] --out PREFIX`
  It writes PREFIX.md and PREFIX.json.
- Input TSV columns: bench, arm, task_id, run, token, finish_reason, started, completion_tokens.
- Converter for the main session's evaluation cells:
  `cells_to_long.py OUT.tsv NoSkill='<glob>' Seed='<glob>' Final='<glob>'`
  The latest attempt with a verdict wins.
- The library slots in beside readout.Readings, which already provides the shared-draw paired cluster bootstrap and unknown imputation. stage_table adds the analytic cross-check, discordant counts, exact p, Holm, noise floor, MDE, truncation bounds and the occasion audit.

STANDING SENTINEL (v4/v5)
- Every evaluation and gate round interleaves a fixed panel: 20 SearchQA + 20 OfficeQA training items × the scaffold text × 1 run.
- Its terse share and pass rate identify the serving regime.
- A regime mismatch with the reference window voids cross-window comparisons; within-round contrasts are labelled with the regime.

pilot.result: No paid pilot was needed. The template and its verification run entirely on existing training cells: 0 model calls. The one open empirical question the work raised is the serving-regime switch. The proposed answer is the standing sentinel, which is a harness change for the main session or v4, not a one-off pilot. A one-off probe now would see only the current regime and could not validate that the sentinel tracks regime switches; that needs probes spread across hours.
pilot.blocked_by: Not blocked by permissions; no paid call was attempted. The owner's 05:59 HKT reporting cutoff made a multi-hour regime-tracking probe impractical in this session.
pilot.command: Sentinel, to be added inside each round's dispatch, interleaved with the round's arms: 20 SearchQA + 20 OfficeQA TRAINING items × the scaffold text × 1 run, recording completion_tokens and the verdict. Read it with: python3 -I -B scripts2/stage_table.py sentinel_long.tsv --final sentinel@roundX --noskill sentinel@reference --out sentinel_check (the terse-share and pass-rate shift). Estimated cost about 0.23M tokens per round (20 × 3.4k + 20 × 8k).

risks:
- Variance components come from TRAINING items. Test-panel floors and detectable effects are estimates.
- The SpreadsheetBench π_rep = 0.20 comes from about 15 items with 2 runs, so its floor (±6.2) and MDE (8.9-9.2) are weak. LiveMath rests on 100 items and ALFWorld on 57.
- Coverage was checked under a multinomial model for single runs and resampling from the bank, at discordance ≥ 8%. For near-identical Skills with fewer than 10 discordant items, R3 switches to the Tango interval, but small-discordance coverage was not separately enumerated.
- The serving-regime mechanism is unknown. It is not explained by reasoning output, model name or request bytes. Regimes may shift with deployments; the sentinel detects them but cannot remove them.
- Effects can be regime-specific: a −6.0-point interaction was measured on a real contrast. A paper claim needs either measurement in two windows or an explicit regime qualifier.
- I could not check whether the v3 test cells for NoSkill-ds, I-ds and E-ds were co-scheduled, because the hard rules forbid me to read them. If they were not, the existing v3 Δ vs NoSkill numbers (especially OfficeQA) may carry a regime term of the measured size (6-24 points).
- Holm over 10 cells is conservative. D8 may pre-register a smaller primary family.
- The OfficeQA test-panel cluster structure is unknown to me. On training, clustering changed the SE by less than 5%.
- The earlier attempt's work was reused after an audit, not rebuilt from scratch. The audit covered file-size identity, the path guard, a 42/42 test re-run, exact reproduction of the registered analysis, and an independent end-to-end re-run on the new machine.
cost_estimate:
- This exploration: 0 model tokens; about 3 CPU-minutes locally and remotely.
- Running the template on any run's cells: free.
- Standing sentinel: about 0.23M tokens per round (20 SearchQA × about 3.4k + 20 OfficeQA × about 8k, ESTIMATED from context §6 and the measured mean charged tokens: OfficeQA seed 7.9k, scaffold 4.7k).
- Placebo arm at the final stage (and likewise an optional same-window replicate arm): about 1,035 cells, the documented size of one five-bench test evaluation. That is about 4M tokens without ALFWorld, plus about 4-14M with ALFWorld. ALFWorld training cells average 28,463 (scaffold) to 106,073 (seed) charged tokens per cell, measured.
- Re-running a non-co-scheduled test contrast interleaved costs one arm per bench (about 1.4M tokens for SearchQA's 400 cells, about 1.4M for OfficeQA's 172).
recommendation:
1. Adopt the template (R1-R12) for every stage table and for the paper. The headline column is Δ vs task-card Seed, paired, with up/down counts, exact p (Holm over 10 cells), noise floor and MDE80 on every row. Report Δ vs NoSkill as context only, because placebo text alone moves scores −9.8 to +3.6 points.

2. Before the main session publishes the v3 stage table:
   - Run scripts2/cells_to_long.py on the NoSkill-ds, I-ds and E-ds evaluation cells, then scripts2/stage_table.py.
   - Read the "Co-scheduled" column first. Any Δ between arms dispatched in different windows gets "not co-scheduled, no CI" until it is re-measured interleaved.
   - Mark stages 1-5 as "reused, Δ ≡ 0 by construction" (0 rules accepted).
   - Show OfficeQA's truncation bounds (I-ds 48.3% lower bound, 57.0% ceiling).

3. v4/v5 harness:
   - Interleave all arms of a comparison in one window.
   - Add the 40-cell sentinel to every round.
   - Never compare across rounds or chains without a same-window re-measurement. The v3 confirm already re-measures the parent, which is good.

4. Pre-register claims where power exists. Per-bench MDE80 at test is 3.5-10 points, the macro about 3.8. A +4-point method effect should be claimed on the macro row or on a similar-target pair, not per bench. Raising runs per item from 1 to 4 narrows intervals by only about 21% at four times the cost, so it is not the power fix; more items are.

5. Never use the percentile bootstrap on trigger panels of 20 items or fewer (coverage 48-93%). Use exact randomization there (D8).

6. Adding a placebo arm (Seed + matched-length irrelevant text) at the final stage costs about 4M tokens without ALFWorld. It turns "learned rule beats a good instruction" into a claim that excludes the any-text effect.
references:
- Miller, E. (2024). Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations. arXiv:2411.00640. Verified in the HTML version, 2026-10-21: Eq. 1 (SE), Eq. 4 (clustered SE), Eq. 7 (paired SE), Eq. 9 (sample size), Eq. 10 (MDE); Sec. 3.1 resampling factor (1+2/K)/3 in the uniform-difficulty example; five recommendations.
- Bowyer, S., Aitchison, L., Ivanova, D. R. (2025). Position: Don't Use the CLT in LLM Evals With Fewer Than a Few Hundred Datapoints. ICML 2025 spotlight position paper, arXiv:2503.01747. Wilson or Bayesian intervals for single proportions (Sec. 3.1); clustered Bayesian model (Sec. 3.2); paired Bayesian method for paired comparisons at small N (Sec. 3.4).
- Madaan, L., Singh, A. K., Schaeffer, R., Poulton, A., Koyejo, S., Stenetorp, P., Narang, S., Hupkes, D. (2024). Quantifying Variance in Evaluation Benchmarks. arXiv:2406.10229. Seed variance across training initialisations; completion framing reduces variance for 7B models; IRT-style methods struggle to reduce variance.
- Newcombe, R. G. (1998). Improved confidence intervals for the difference between binomial proportions based on paired data. Statistics in Medicine 17:2635-2650, method 10 and Table III (reproduced to 4 decimals).
- Tango, T. (1998). Equivalence test and confidence interval for the difference in proportions for the paired-sample design. Statistics in Medicine 17:891-908. Matches repo skillopt/active_evidence/matched.py.
- Holm, S. (1979). A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics 6:65-70.
- Chen, L., Zaharia, M., Zou, J. (2023). How is ChatGPT's behavior changing over time? arXiv:2307.09009. Precedent for occasion and serving drift.
- He, H. and Thinking Machines (2025-09-10). Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference. Batch-invariance explains temperature-0 token-level nondeterminism.
- Project sources:
  - docs/handoff/cal1-registration-20261020.md: arm definitions and registered A2/A3/A5 results.
  - docs/handoff/coevo5-v1-results-20261019.md: test denominators 400/172/125/279 (about 197-200 qualified)/134, and the current per-arm table format.
  - skillopt/coevo5/readout.py: the existing shared-draw paired cluster bootstrap and unknown imputation.
